notes: Researched 27 Sep 2026 (Asia/Kolkata). Source S1 is linked from https://neet.nta.nic.in/ (Public Notices) as 'KEY DATA POINTS OF NEET (UG) OVER YEARS'; the document prints no date of its own — publishedOn 2026-07-16 is the upload date in its NTA file path (uploads/2026/07/20260716…), the same day as NTA's result press release (https://cdnbbsr.s3waas.gov.in/s37bc1ec1d9c3426357e69acd5bf320061/uploads/2026/07/20260716477215762.pdf, 16 July 2026), which says 'Category-wise cut-off marks and percentiles are being published simultaneously.' The press release itself has a text layer but carries NO cut-off table. Table 8 on page 3 of S1 ('The category-wise number of candidates qualified, based on qualifying criteria of NEET (UG)- 2024, 2025 and 2026.') prints, per category, the qualifying percentile criterion and, per year, a 'Marks range' (highest-lowest) and 'Total Candidates'. 'marks' here is the LOWER end of the printed range (e.g. 2026 UR/EWS '715-213' -> 213), i.e. the lowest qualifying mark out of 720; the percentile criterion and the full range stay in the evidence line. NEET (UG) 2026 figures are for the re-examination held on 21 June 2026 (NTA public notice 15 May 2026; toppers list title '(Held on 21st June, 2026)'). Values were read by eye off a 170-dpi render of page 3 (scratchpad neet_cut_zoom.png); ST & PwBD 2026 is printed '191-177' while OBC/SC & PwBD are '193-177' — copied as printed. S1 is a scan with NO text layer, so scripts/import-official-cutoffs.ts cannot prove these rows and will print FAIL for every one (no OCR, by rule); separately, a marks-range cell ('715-213') is not a plain number for the grid proof, and the text proof needs the figure right after the label. Nothing here is written until the main session decides on a reviewed path for scanned official documents.
